title: Who really came second?
hook: The champion is crowned after 7 matches. Do you need a whole new contest for second place?

knows: finding the biggest by comparing two at a time
doesNotKnow: that a knockout bracket leaves a short list of candidates for second place

misconception: After finding the champion of 8 you must search the other 7 again to find the second best.
objective: The learner can explain that the second best can only have lost to the champion, so it is one of the 3 players the champion beat; 2 more matches find it, 9 in all rather than 13.

claims.text: With 8 players in knockout rounds, the champion is found in 7 matches and plays 3 of them.
claims.source: Each match knocks out one player and 7 must go (8 - 1); there are log2 8 = 3 rounds and the champion plays one match per round. Demo.tsx playAll().

claims.text: The second best can only lose to the best, so it must be one of the players the champion beat; anyone who lost to someone else lost to a stronger player who is not the champion.
claims.source: Proof by contradiction: if the second best lost to X and X is not the champion, X is stronger than the second best and weaker than the champion, impossible. Builder checked over 3,000 random brackets (seeded): always exactly 3 candidates, true second always among them.

claims.text: On this bracket the true second best, F, was knocked out in round 1, not D, the final's loser.
claims.source: Demo.tsx STRENGTH = [3, 5, 1, 6, 8, 7, 2, 4] for A-H, chosen (not random) so that the runner-up meets the champion in round 1. In a random bracket the second best reaches the final only when seeded in the other half from the champion (4 of the 7 other positions).

claims.text: 2 more matches among the 3 candidates find the runner-up: 9 matches in all, instead of 7 + 6 = 13 by searching the other 7 again.
claims.source: Largest of 3 needs 2 comparisons; largest of 7 needs 6 (arithmetic). Knuth, The Art of Computer Programming Vol. 3, 5.3.3 treats selecting the second largest (n + ceil(log2 n) - 2 comparisons; 9 for n = 8). Not claimed as optimal on the stage.

recall.question: A 16-team knockout cup has just crowned its champion. To find the true second-best team fairly, which teams need to play again?
options: Only the 4 teams the champion beat
recall.why: The second best can only have lost to the champion, and the champion played 4 matches (log2 16), so only those 4 teams are candidates.
